newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Posta Bank hit by panic withdrawals.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Posta Bank hit by panic withdrawals.

text.p: Hungary's Posta Bank was hit by thousands of depositors rushing to withdraw their savings on Friday, but regulators said there was no justification for the panic.
People queued for hours outside Posta Bank branch offices to withdraw their money after rumours circulated that the bank had big losses.
But bank officials said denied the rumours that the bank was in trouble, and an official of Hungary's banking supervision said the panic was not justified.
Zoltan Pacsi, vice chairman of the Banking Supervision, said a recent investigation of the privately owned bank had turned up no major problems.
"According to our knowledge, the banking supervision did not find any problems at Posta Bank, which would justify the current panic," Pacsi said.
At a hastily-convened news conference Posta Bank's chairman, Gabor Princz, also denied that the bank was in difficulty.

"It is not true news that Posta Bank has financial problems, but it is partly true that there are rumours spreading in Budapest. And it has a damaging effect on the bank," Princz told Hungarian Radio.

"I have to say that Posta Bank has been operating for nine years, and I hope everyone is satisfied with our services," he said, adding that the bank had no plans to freeze accounts and would continue to pay out to depositors.
Bank officials said they could not give estimates of amounts that had been withdrawn, but queues of up to 500 depositors at a time jammed bank offices throughout the city.
Posta Bank is Hungary's third largest financial institution and has a wide branch system, operating in part out of the nation's post offices.
In March of last year it reported a pre-tax profit of 2.832 billion HUF and had a balance sheet total of almost 270 billion forints at the end of 1995, up from 200.7 billion for 1994.

Major foreign shareholders listed in 1996 were Osterreichische Postsparkasse with 10.4 percent, EA-Generali with seven percent and Wiener Allianz with 0.2 percent. Other shareholders included GiroCredit, Volksbank and C.Trieste.
